content.problemStatement:
We have a wooden plank of the length `n` **units**. Some ants are walking on the plank, each ant moves with a speed of **1 unit per second**. Some of the ants move to the **left**, the other move to the **right**.

When two ants moving in two **different** directions meet at some point, they change their directions and continue moving again. Assume changing directions does not take any additional time.

When an ant reaches **one end** of the plank at a time `t`, it falls out of the plank immediately.

With an integer `n` and two integer arrays `left` and `right`, the positions of the ants moving to the left and the right, output *the moment when the last ant(s) fall out of the plank*.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/06/17/ants.jpg)

```
Input: n = 4, left = [4,3], right = [0,1]
Output: 4
Explanation: In the image above:
-The ant at index 0 is named A and going to the right.
-The ant at index 1 is named B and going to the right.
-The ant at index 3 is named C and going to the left.
-The ant at index 4 is named D and going to the left.
The last moment when an ant was on the plank is t = 4 seconds. After that, it falls immediately out of the plank. (i.e., We can say that at t = 4.0000000001, there are no ants on the plank).
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/06/17/ants2.jpg)

```
Input: n = 7, left = [], right = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]
Output: 7
Explanation: All ants are going to the right, the ant at index 0 needs 7 seconds to fall.
```

**Example 3:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/06/17/ants3.jpg)

```
Input: n = 7, left = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7], right = []
Output: 7
Explanation: All ants are going to the left, the ant at index 7 needs 7 seconds to fall.
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= n <= 10^4`
* `0 <= left.length <= n + 1`
* `0 <= left[i] <= n`
* `0 <= right.length <= n + 1`
* `0 <= right[i] <= n`
* `1 <= left.length + right.length <= n + 1`
* All values of `left` and `right` are unique, and each value can appear **only in one** of the two arrays.

notes: The collision rule can be ignored because swapping directions when identical ants meet produces the same set of fall times as letting the ants pass through each other.
Use 0 when there are no left-moving ants and n when there are no right-moving ants.
solution.approach: For ants moving left, the time to fall is exactly their position. For ants moving right, the time to fall is n minus their position. When ants collide and reverse direction, this is equivalent to ants passing through each other, so the last fall time is the maximum of the two sets of fall times.

better.complexity: O(left.length + right.length) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
better.description: Observe that when two ants moving in opposite directions meet, exchanging their identities is equivalent to letting them pass through each other. Therefore, only the original direction and position of each ant matter for its fall time.

optimal.complexity: O(left.length + right.length) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: For every ant moving left from position x, its fall time is x. For every ant moving right from position x, its fall time is n - x. Return the maximum of these values. Empty direction arrays are handled with defaults of 0 for left and n for right.

bruteForce.complexity: O(T) simulation time per ant in a straightforward time-step simulation, where T is the number of simulated time steps; this can be much larger than necessary.
bruteForce.description: Simulate every ant's movement until it reaches an endpoint, while handling direction changes at collisions. This is unnecessary because collisions only exchange the identities of the ants.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n + left.length + right.length), which is O(n) under the problem constraints.

followUps: Why can collisions be ignored without changing the last falling time?
How would the approach change if ants moved at different speeds?
What additional information would be needed if the problem asked which ant falls last rather than only the time?
